answer: Each identity maintains one jetty willow-plank section for a 70-credit bond. It coats them with raven-grade tar, logging drums; the auditor samples thickness, multiplies drums by volume, checks it against the log, and a shortfall burns the bond. The coat must be raven grade at the listed thickness; wrong grade fails even if volume matches. First section 31, kth 31+6(k-1), 1000th 6025; 1000 false sections cost 3,028,000 plus 70,000 locked. A rented-tar ring fails: the log carries the owner's key, not the claimant's. An honest maintainer pays 31 once and reclaims the bond after a clean epoch.
